name: spatial-linkage
title: Spatial Linkage — Model -> AS -> GLB Scene-Node Links
question:
For each biomodel-DO organ annotation, exactly which ASCT+B-3D crosswalk
GLB scene node(s) does it correspond to — precise enough for a 3D viewer
to color/label the right node per model?

study_card.goal: Join biomodel-DO organ annotations to crosswalk anatomical-structure nodes on shared Uberon CURIE, and confirm the composite loads a non-empty per-link list plus summary counts.
study_card.mechanism: SpatialLinkStep.update -> build_spatial_links(query, max_results) = build_biomodel_do_catalog(...) organs joined against fetch_crosswalk(...) rows sharing the same Uberon -> links + spatial_link_summary -> RAMEmitter.
study_card.expected_result: At least one (biomodel, crosswalk AS node) link, each carrying the exact `node_name` a viewer should color; `readout` is a placeholder string in v1 (no simulation output wired yet).
study_card.main_expert_question: Is Uberon-CURIE-only join precise enough (a model's organ can link to multiple GLB nodes cut from the same reference-organ GLB), or does a real viewer need a single 'best' node resolved per model?

biological_summary:
Marking an organ "covered" is a coarse signal; a 3D viewer needs to know
exactly which GLB scene node to color for a given model. This study joins
each biomodel-DO organ annotation directly to the crosswalk rows sharing
its Uberon CURIE, producing the (model, GLB node) pairs a viewer renders
against. Because HRA ships separate male/female reference-organ GLBs, one
organ annotation legitimately links to two nodes (one per sex) — the join
is deliberately Uberon-only in v1, deferring "pick the single best node"
resolution to a future viewer-side step.
readouts: per-link node_name (the GLB scene node a model's organ maps to)

report.title: Spatial Linkage — 10 model->AS->node links across 5 models, liver + pancreas
report.objective:
For each glucose-regulation biomodel-DO organ annotation, which
ASCT+B-3D crosswalk GLB scene node(s) does it join to, precisely enough
for a 3D viewer to color the right node per model?
report.conclusion:
The live join produces 10 links across 5 distinct biomodels (25-result
"glucose regulation" query): BIOMD0000000633 (Bulik2016 hepatic glucose
metabolism) -> VH_F_liver/VH_M_liver; MODEL2001080002 (Topp2000 b-cell
mass/insulin/glucose), MODEL1112110004 (Silber2007 IV glucose), and
BIOMD0000000382 (Sturis1991 ultradian oscillations) and
BIOMD0000000372 (Tolic2000 insulin-glucose feedback) each ->
VH_F_pancreas/VH_M_pancreas. Every model links to exactly 2 nodes (one
per sex), confirming the Uberon-only join fires correctly and is fully
reproducible from the shared organ Uberon.
report.caveat:
`readout` is a literal placeholder string (`"pending time-series"`) in
v1 for every link — no simulation output is wired to a node yet, so
this study demonstrates the join topology only, not a live-data 3D
viewer. The 2-links-per-model pattern (one per sex) also means a
viewer must still resolve "which sex's GLB is currently displayed" to
color a single node, not both.

findings.statement:
The live Uberon-only join produces 10 (model, GLB-node) links across
5 distinct biomodels, with every model linking to exactly 2 nodes
(one per sex) -- confirming the join mechanism is deterministic and
reproducible from the shared organ Uberon, even though `readout` is
still a literal placeholder string ("pending time-series") for every
link in v1.

evidence.summary: 10 links across 5 models (BIOMD0000000633 -> liver x2; MODEL2001080002, MODEL1112110004, BIOMD0000000382, BIOMD0000000372 -> pancreas x2 each); 2 links per model, one per sex.

regression_compatibility.basis: The baseline spatial-link join composite (biomodel-DO organs x crosswalk rows on shared Uberon) completed without error.

biological_validation.basis: The join topology is verified correct (every model links to exactly 2 sex-split nodes), but `readout` is a placeholder string for every link -- no simulation result is actually linked to a node yet, so this is gated needs_calibration rather than passed.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-01 establishes the join mechanism works reliably (10 links/5 models, Uberon-only, fully reproducible) but carries no result data yet -- model->AS->node linkage works at the topology level only.

limitations: `readout` is a literal placeholder string ('pending time-series') for every link in v1; no simulation output is wired to a node yet.
The 2-links-per-model pattern (one per sex) means a viewer must still resolve 'which sex's GLB is currently displayed' to color a single node, not both.

resolved_uncertainties: Uberon-only join reliably produces exactly 2 links per model (one per sex), confirming the join mechanism is deterministic and reproducible.
remaining_uncertainties: Can we spatially link model RESULTS (steady-state values), not just organ presence, to a specific AS node?
Is Uberon-CURIE-only join precise enough, or does a real viewer need a single 'best' node resolved per model?

followup_study_proposals.title: Result-driven spatial linkage
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Color AS nodes by a real model readout (steady-state concentration from the corpus dataset) instead of a placeholder string, so the 3D viewer shows results, not just coverage.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: Extract steady-state species concentrations from the committed corpus COPASI/Tellurium comparison dataset and attach them as the `readout` field on each (model, AS-node) link, replacing the placeholder 'pending time-series' string; re-render the 3D viewer pack colored by that value.

alternative_hypotheses.discriminated_by: the two nodes per model are exactly the female/male GLBs of the same organ (VH_F/VH_M liver or pancreas), matching HRA's sex-split reference organs -- the expected behavior, not a bug.

alternative_hypotheses.claim: The links might already carry model results.
alternative_hypotheses.discriminated_by: every link's readout is the literal placeholder 'pending time-series'; wiring a real steady-state value is the fp-result-driven-spatial-link follow-up.
